programme: Master of Arts in Children and Adolescent Counseling

parts.title: Foundations of Counseling Theory
parts.blurb: The intellectual scaffolding on which professional counseling practice is built: what a theory is, what it does, where it comes from, how it is evaluated, and how it must be adapted to the developmental and cultural realities of children and adolescents.

chapters.title: The Role of Theory in Professional Counseling Practice
chapters.subtitle: Why theory matters, what it does and does not do, and how it becomes a working instrument in the counseling room.

chapters.title: Scientific and Professional Foundations of Counseling
chapters.subtitle: The research tradition, the professional identity, and the movements that established counseling as a distinct discipline.

chapters.title: Philosophical Worldviews: The Five Domains of Theory
chapters.subtitle: Humanistic, cognitive, behavioral, systemic, and constructivist assumptions examined side by side.

chapters.title: A Genealogy of Counseling Theories
chapters.subtitle: A historical map from the late nineteenth century to the contemporary integrative era.

chapters.title: The Therapeutic Relationship: Alliance, Rupture, and Repair
chapters.subtitle: The common substrate on which all theory-specific methods rest.

chapters.title: Common Factors, Placebo Effects, and Specific Factors
chapters.subtitle: What all therapies share, what is unique to each, and why the distinction matters for ethical practice.

chapters.title: The Evidence Base: Evaluating Counseling Theories
chapters.subtitle: Outcome research, treatment manuals, and the appraisal of efficacy for youth-serving interventions.

chapters.title: Culturally Responsive Theory and the Cultural Lens
chapters.subtitle: Culture as a constitutive element of personality, not a variable added to it.

chapters.title: Developmental Foundations for Counseling Youth
chapters.subtitle: The developmental science that constrains and informs any theory applied to children and adolescents.

parts.title: Person-Centered and Humanistic Theories
parts.blurb: Theories that locate the person, not the problem, at the centre of change: the growth-oriented traditions inaugurated by Carl Rogers and extended by existential, Gestalt, phenomenological, and dialogical thinkers.

chapters.title: Person-Centered Theory: The Client as Expert
chapters.subtitle: Rogers' theory of the self, the actualising tendency, and the conditions of therapeutic change.

chapters.title: Existential Therapy: Meaning, Isolation, and Freedom
chapters.subtitle: Yalom, May, Frankl, and the clinical use of existential confrontation.

chapters.title: Gestalt Therapy: Awareness, Contact, and the Here and Now
chapters.subtitle: Perls, Foulkes, and the experimental phenomenology of the counseling session.

chapters.title: Focusing-Oriented Therapy and the Felt Sense
chapters.subtitle: Gendlin's experiential method and the therapeutic use of bodily felt meaning.

chapters.title: Transactional Analysis: Structure, Strategy, and Script
chapters.subtitle: Berne's ego-state model, the drama triangle, and the adapted use of TA with young people.

chapters.title: Internal Family Systems and Structural Dissociation
chapters.subtitle: Schwarz's model of parts and the treatment of partitioned experience in traumatized youth.

parts.title: Cognitive Theories
parts.blurb: The cognitive family of theories: the proposition that mental activity is mediated by the appraisal of events, the examination of belief systems, and the third-wave movement that loosened the grip of rational disputation.

chapters.title: Cognitive Therapy: The Cognitive Model
chapters.subtitle: Aaron Beck's theory of depression and anxiety, the cognitive conceptualization triangle, and the disciplined practice of cognitive therapy.

chapters.title: Cognitive Therapy with Children and Adolescents
chapters.subtitle: Developmental adaptations, the role of the parent, and the modification of thought records for younger clients.

chapters.title: Rational Emotive Behavior Therapy
chapters.subtitle: Ellis's ABC model, the disputing process, and rational emotional flexibility in the counseling room.

chapters.title: Schema Therapy: Modes, Styles, and Early Maladaptive Schemas
chapters.subtitle: Young's model of personality organisation and the schema-focused treatment of adolescents.

chapters.title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy
chapters.subtitle: Psychological flexibility, the hexaflex, and defusion in adolescent work.

chapters.title: Dialectical Behavior Therapy and Its Adolescent Adaptations
chapters.subtitle: Linehan's biosocial theory, the four modules, and dialectical strategies in practice.

chapters.title: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy and Mindfulness Approaches
chapters.subtitle: MBSR, MBCT, and the cultivation of attentional flexibility in young people.

parts.title: Behavioral Theories
parts.blurb: The behavioral tradition: learning as the engine of change, the systematic analysis of behaviour, and the translation of learning principles into interventions that can be measured, replicated, and evaluated.

chapters.title: Behavior Therapy: Principles of Learning
chapters.subtitle: Classical and operant conditioning, the law of effect, and the epistemology of observable behaviour.

chapters.title: Applied Behavior Analysis: Functional Assessment
chapters.subtitle: The ABC model, functional analysis, and the construction of hypotheses about why a behaviour occurs.

chapters.title: Exposure, Modeling, and Behavioral Skills Training
chapters.subtitle: The treatment of avoidance, fear, and deficit through systematic desensitisation, observation, and rehearsal.

chapters.title: Operant Conditioning and Contingency Management
chapters.subtitle: Reinforcement, schedules, and the deliberate shaping of behaviour in clinical and educational settings.

chapters.title: Behavioral Activation and Activity Scheduling
chapters.subtitle: The behavioural treatment of depression and withdrawal in adolescents.

chapters.title: Contingency Management in Schools and Clinics
chapters.subtitle: Token systems, behaviour contracts, and the negotiated restructuring of reinforcement in real settings.

chapters.title: Functional Analysis of Self-Injurious and Aggressive Behaviour
chapters.subtitle: Safety-oriented assessment and intervention with behaviour that is harmful or dangerous.

parts.title: Systemic, Family, and Relational Theories
parts.blurb: Theories that locate the individual inside a network of relationships and meanings: the systemic turn, the family as the unit of treatment, and the narrative and solution-oriented traditions.

chapters.title: Family Systems Theory: Bowen and the Generational Project
chapters.subtitle: Differentiation, triangles, nuclear family emotional process, and the genogram as a clinical tool.

chapters.title: Structural Family Therapy
chapters.subtitle: Minuchin's structural model, boundaries, subsystems, and restructuring with adolescents and parents.

chapters.title: Strategic Family Therapy and Communication Theory
chapters.subtitle: Problem-maintaining sequences, directives, and the reframing of the problem.

chapters.title: Family Therapy with Parents and Adolescents
chapters.subtitle: Developmental and systemic consultation with families in conflict.

chapters.title: Attachment Theory and Attachment-Based Therapy
chapters.subtitle: Bowlby, Ainsworth, and the translation of attachment research into treatment.

chapters.title: Solution-Focused Brief Therapy and Strength-Based Practice
chapters.subtitle: Scaling, exception questions, and the deliberate use of what is already working.

chapters.title: Narrative Therapy and the Re-Authoring of Lives
chapters.subtitle: Externalisation, unique outcomes, and the collaborative reconstruction of adolescent identity.

parts.title: Emotional, Trauma-Informed, and Somatic Practice
parts.blurb: Theories and methods that work with feeling, with the body, and with the developmental consequences of threat: emotion-focused work, trauma-informed phases, bilateral stimulation, and somatic regulation.

chapters.title: Emotion-Focused Therapy
chapters.subtitle: Greenberg's model of emotion regulation, the change point, and emotion-focused work with youth in distress.

chapters.title: Trauma-Informed Practice: Principles, Phases, and Precautions
chapters.subtitle: The neurobiology of threat, the three-phase model, and the ethical floor rules of trauma work.

chapters.title: EMDR and Bilateral Stimulation
chapters.subtitle: Shapiro's protocol, the adaptive information processing model, and careful adaptation for children.

chapters.title: Stabilisation, Grounding, and Phase-Oriented Work
chapters.subtitle: Skills for the first phase of trauma treatment and the maintenance of stability between sessions.

chapters.title: Interpersonal Psychotherapy for Adolescents
chapters.subtitle: Klerman's model, the social problem-solving curriculum, and the treatment of adolescent depression.

chapters.title: Mentalization-Based Treatment
chapters.subtitle: Fonagy's model of mentalizing, the not-knowing stance, and epistemic trust.

chapters.title: Somatic, Sensorimotor, and Polyvagal-Informed Practice
chapters.subtitle: Body-based approaches, autonomic regulation, and the neuroception of safety.

parts.title: Motivational, Social, Developmental, and Cultural Theories
parts.blurb: Theories that attend to motivation, to social learning, to development, and to the cultural and gendered location of the person in the world.

chapters.title: Motivational Interviewing
chapters.subtitle: Miller and Rollnick's four processes, change talk, and the adolescent adaptation of a conversational method.

chapters.title: Social Cognitive Learning Theory
chapters.subtitle: Bandura's reciprocal determinism, self-efficacy, and the modelling of behaviour in social contexts.

chapters.title: Adolescent Development: Theory and Counseling Implications
chapters.subtitle: Identity, autonomy, risk, and peer relations as a developmental framework for intervention.

chapters.title: Psychodynamic and Object Relations Approaches
chapters.subtitle: The relational substrate of personality, transference, and developmental lines of interpretation.

chapters.title: Multicultural, Feminist, and Intersectional Theory
chapters.subtitle: Power, voice, and privilege in the counseling relationship and in the theories that inform it.

chapters.title: Affirmative Practice with LGBTQ+ Youth
chapters.subtitle: Gender-responsive and affirming practice, the role of the therapeutic alliance, and the harms of conversion practices.

chapters.title: Resilience, Ecological Systems, and Strengths-Based Practice
chapters.subtitle: Bronfenbrenner, Masten's resilience research, and the systematic mobilisation of protective factors.

parts.title: Integration, Assessment, and Professional Practice
parts.blurb: The working core of the course: how theories are integrated into a coherent stance, how cases are conceptualised, how progress is measured, and how the course itself is taught and assessed.

chapters.title: Theoretical Integration and the Integrative Stance
chapters.subtitle: Technical eclecticism, assimilative integration, and the discipline of a coherent theory of change.

chapters.title: Case Conceptualization and Treatment Planning
chapters.subtitle: The five-part formulation, the mechanism of change, and the written treatment plan.

chapters.title: Assessment and Outcome Monitoring in Counseling
chapters.subtitle: Instruments, session notes, measurement-based care, and the ethical use of assessment data.

chapters.title: Termination, Evaluation, and the Ethics of Endings
chapters.subtitle: Planned termination, relapse prevention, transfer, and the evaluation of outcome.

chapters.title: Teletherapy and Technology in Counseling with Youth
chapters.subtitle: Secure video practice, telehealth with minors, and digital ethics.

chapters.title: School Counseling Practice and Consultation
chapters.subtitle: The school counselor's role, the consultation model, and the ethics of working in an institutional setting.

chapters.title: Teaching CAC. 701: Session Plans and Facilitation
chapters.subtitle: A complete teaching sequence for the course, including delivery notes, activities, and assessment alignment.

chapters.title: Assessment Blueprint, Assignments, and Rubrics
chapters.subtitle: Course-level assessment design, major assignments, grading rubrics, and the assurance of academic integrity.
